spin.situation: Right now, when something gets captured (a YouTube link, a note, an idea) the write-up often doesn't happen right away — the backlog literally says 'knowledge note pending — I'll write it next session.'
spin.problem: There's a gap between the moment something is captured and the moment it actually becomes useful. The system 'presses the gas' (captures) but the 'power' (the finished note) only arrives later, in a batch, if at all.
spin.implication: Every capture sitting in that gap is a small silent failure to deliver — and it's the exact HIGH-priority problem already flagged. Left alone, captures pile up and get processed in a rushed batch, or forgotten.
spin.need_payoff: Instead of batching write-ups for 'next session', do a tiny bit of processing at capture time — even a one-line stub — so there's never a cold start; the system stays primed between captures the way a race turbo stays spun up between corners.

source_evidence.quote: If I stay on the gas and press the brake, you slow down for the corner and the turbo keeps spinning.
source_evidence.named_mechanism: anti-lag: maintaining turbo spool during throttle-off periods via a secondary input

candidates.transfer_reasoning: Invariant: a system with response latency avoids that latency not by being bigger/faster but by never fully idling — a cheap secondary input keeps the expensive resource primed between demands. Fusion's Gateway capture pipeline has the same shape: capture is instant, synthesis (the knowledge note) is expensive and deferred to a batch, so it always cold-starts. The fix is the same shape as anti-lag: a cheap, continuous secondary action (auto-stub at capture time) that keeps the note partially warm so the full write-up is a top-up, not a cold start.

spin.need_payoff: Add a one-line 'intent' note next to each literal item in these checklists (why the rule exists, what it's meant to prevent), so a reviewer can flag 'technically compliant but violates intent' directly, without needing a live incident to reveal the gap first.
